subject: Re: ROAR benchmark kickoff — scoring interpretability methods
body: Wrap-up decisions from the readout. The sweep completed inside the June window and the report is in Evalline. Headline: two of the five estimators are defensible for sensitive-domain use; plain gradient saliency is formally indistinguishable from random removal at every fraction, and we're recommending teams stop using it for feature-importance claims. Decisions: (1) the ROAR report becomes a standing Evalline module — Tomas's team takes ownership of reruns, and we hand off by June 26; (2) we cut the planned CIFAR extension — ImageNet-scale evidence was the ask, and adding small-scale results doesn't change any decision; (3) Efe writes the one-page guidance doc for the three product teams. Handoff before the OKR lock keeps this off our Q3 plate entirely. Good, clean project. — Dmitri
